title: IN-AG-PFIC-001 has six canon-set homes stating a different rule, and in-review checks the wrong one
body:
**`IN-AG-PFIC-001` MEANS ONE THING IN THE RULE THAT OWNS IT AND A DIFFERENT THING IN SIX CANON-SET HOMES, AND ONE OF THE SIX IS AN ENFORCEMENT CHECKLIST THAT THEREFORE REPORTS THE RULE ENFORCED WHEN IT WAS NEVER EXAMINED.**

FOUND 2026-09-02 by ic reading `AC-00.8` (ST0065). Corroborated the same evening by vc from their own live session context.

## THE TWO READINGS

**OWNER** -- `intent/plugins/claude/rules/agnostic/pfic/RULE.md`: title *Pure Function, Impure Coordination*. An ARCHITECTURAL rule: keep the domain core deterministic and side-effect-free; push I/O, time, randomness and external calls out to the boundary; coordinators compose pure functions and handle the effects.

**THE SIX HOMES**: *Pure-Functional-Idiomatic-Coordination; pattern match, pipe, tag, compose.* A STYLE rule about functional idiom.

**THESE ARE NOT TWO WORDINGS OF ONE RULE. THEY ARE TWO RULES.** Code can satisfy the second completely -- pattern-matched, piped, tagged, composed -- while violating the first outright, because idiom says nothing about where the I/O lives.

## THE SIX HOMES, AND WHY THREE OF THEM ARE MORE THAN UNTIDINESS

1. `intent/plugins/claude/skills/in-review/SKILL.md:54` -- **THE LIVE DEFECT.** The review checklist reads `IN-AG-PFIC-001 -- pattern-match, pipe, tagged-tuple, compose idioms in play`. **A reviewer checks idiom, finds it, and records this rule as CHECKED while I/O sits three calls deep in a domain core.** An instrument that reports a rule enforced when it was never examined -- the vacuous-instrument class, in the estate's own review path.
2. `lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md:191` -- **THE FLEET TEMPLATE.** Every Intent project receives the fork at init and inherits it on every `agents sync`.
3. `intent/plugins/claude/rules/lua/code/dispatch-table-over-if-chain/RULE.md:177` -- **INSIDE THE RULE LIBRARY.** A Lua rule glosses the agnostic principle it cites with the wrong expansion, so the library contradicts its own agnostic pack.
4. `intent/plugins/claude/skills/in-standards/SKILL.md:27` -- the skill whose job is loading these four principles. **vc confirmed this is what loaded into their session at boot tonight, so every node working this project all evening has been holding the wrong rule.**
5. `AGENTS.md:131` (this project, generated from home 2).
6. `intent/plugins/agents/templates/_default/RULES.md:10` -- laid down at fresh init.

Also present, non-canon and not part of this issue: `intent/llm/RULES.md:10` and a v2 blog draft.

## DIVERGENCE AT BIRTH, NOT DRIFT -- CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED

`RULE.md` has carried *Pure Function, Impure Coordination* since its creating commit `1743fa88` (ST0034 WP04) and **has never been renamed**. The two readings were never in agreement at any point. **So this cannot be dismissed as drift somebody will fix in passing, and no copy of this rule has ever once been correct in this estate.**

## WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT

`AT-00.1` compares canon documents against rule SUMMARIES for a 12-word verbatim span. **This fork shares almost no words with the summary it contradicts, and four of its six homes are skills and templates, which are not in that instrument's population at all.** The paraphrase half of `AC-00.1` is therefore not only the judgement half -- **it is also the half with the larger population**, which is why the split into `AC-00.8` was not bookkeeping.

## RULED REMEDY (vc, 2026-09-02, under hv's pen)

**THE FIX IS THE POINTER, NOT A BETTER COPY.** The six homes cite `IN-AG-PFIC-001` and stop restating it -- `AC-00.1`'s own mechanism, and the reason that row exists. **A corrected copy is a copy that will be right until the first time nobody remembers it**, and this one was wrong from its creating commit.

**ORDER, BY BLAST RADIUS RATHER THAN EFFORT:**
1. `in-review/SKILL.md` -- it produces false verdicts today.
2. `lib/templates/llm/_AGENTS.md` -- the fleet inherits the fork.
3. The rule library's own cross-reference -- a library contradicting its agnostic pack undermines every rule in it.

**NOT YET EXECUTED.** Raised to hv, because the fix changes what a rule MEANS across the fleet template and the rule library, and ic had already routed that call to hv before vc ruled the shape.
